thread.title: Digital Realty: The One Tech Company Everyone Should Have In Their Portfolio - Digital Realty Trust, Inc. (NYSE:DLR)

author: Matthew Utesch
title: Digital Realty: The One Tech Company Everyone Should Have In Their Portfolio - Digital Realty Trust, Inc. (NYSE:DLR)
text:
Investment Thesis Investing in the field of technology can be intimidating, even for the most well-educated and sophisticated investors. Large tech firms can be an exception to the rule because companies like International Business Machines ( IBM ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) all produce products/services that generate predictable cash flows that allow them to pay consistently increasing dividends. As for the rest of the tech industry, there is a high-level of risk that comes from investing in small- to medium-size firms because they can develop cutting-edge technology only to see it become outdated six months later.
This begs the question, should conservative investors choose to avoid the tech industry (with the exception of the industry behemoths mentioned above) or are there tech companies out there who have safe/steady business models worthy of our capital?
I propose to those reading that Digital Realty Trust ( DLR ) is the answer to the above question. DLR offers exposure to the tech industry and even more importantly, is entirely focused on data centers which generate highly predictable and sustainable cash flows. While the tech industry may be changing rapidly, their overall dependence on well-placed data centers has grown tremendously.
For those who follow my series on John and Jane ( here ), DLR is one of the larger holdings in my client Jane's retirement portfolio and was originally chosen because it offered a compelling yield with strong growth prospects. DLR's focus on providing investors with a reasonable yield and growth prospects make it one of my favorite long-term stocks in Jane's portfolio.
Background DLR is a real estate investment trust (REIT) that focuses on specialty properties such as data centers. DLR currently has 205 data centers up and running:
155 - North America 38 - Europe 12 - Asia Pacific (**18 of the 205 data centers are held as investments in unconsolidated joint ventures) Because of its size, DLR is able to deliver data center solutions ranging from small-scale to entire dedicated buildings. DLR has global reach and has also established an industry record of "10 consecutive years of 5 nines" or 99.999% uptime. As you can imagine, this history is extremely important to firms both large and small who rely on DLR's services to generate revenues and expand their business.
Size and Diversification When it comes to data centers, no other REIT comes close to the size of DLR in terms of market cap and enterprise value.
DLR - market capitalization of $21.8 billion and an enterprise value of $33 billion. CyrusOne ( CONE ) - market capitalization of $5.8 billion and an enterprise value of $7.8 billion. QTS Realty Trust ( QTS ) - market capitalization of $2.0 billion and an enterprise value of $3.5 billion. With a market cap of $21.8 billion, DLR offers reduced risk that comes with an entity this large but still generates meaningful growth that can be difficult to find in other large-cap companies.
Holding the title of being a large-cap company isn't a great reason by itself to claim that the company is less risky. Thankfully, DLR's client diversification brings in revenues from a number of companies across a spectrum of industries.
Source: March Investor Presentation
I think we can all agree that the ever-changing scope and direction of technology can feel intimidating (especially when it comes to investing), but I take comfort in the fact that data centers are continuing to grow in importance for practically all industries.
DLR's ability to serve all companies regardless of size is a huge advantage because it allows them to build relationships and benefit when a small tech firm turns into a large tech firm. Without its size and scope, DLR would not be able to handle many of the requirements of the companies listed above.
Debt One of the biggest concerns for REITs going forward is that an increased cost of capital is likely to eat into funds from operations (FFO) which means investors are likely to see smaller dividend increases going forward. REITs are highly dependent on debt which is why the more variable rate-based debt there is, the more likely it is that FFO growth will slow down (or in the worst case) will begin to reduce FFO.
DLR has positioned itself so that the risk posed by increasing interest rates will have minimal effect on day-to-day operations and FFO generation. For further context, let's compare DLR's credit metrics with that of CONE. DLR's credit can be described by the following:
18% Variable Rate 82% Fixed Rate 100% Unsecured Debt CONE's situation can be described as the following:
45% Variable Rate 55% Fixed Rate 100% Unsecured Debt Although both companies come with 100% unsecured debt (which makes it easier to liquidate/sell properties), you can see that their use of variable-rate debt and fixed rate debt are quite different. With less than 20% of debt tied to a variable-rate, DLR's bottom-line is less susceptible to the short-term and long-term fluctuations in the market.
DLR recently issued $650 million of 4.45% unsecured notes that are due in 2028. These funds are intended to reduce borrowings under the revolving credit facility, develop or acquire other properties, and the potential repayment of other debt/equity securities. I view this move as a smart one largely because DLR's cost to issue debt has not increased even though we have seen a strong movement upwards in the 10-year US Treasury Rate.
Source: March Investor Presentation
The chart above allows us to draw some of the following conclusions:
DLR's cost of issuing senior notes has not increased at the same rate as the 10-Year US Treasury Rate. The tightening of the spread shown above means that DLR still has access to low-cost financing methods. DLR's access to low-cost financing methods shows that the market believes in the quality of the company's operations. DLR's financial strength has allowed them to build a debt maturity timeline that has no material maturities until 2020. Although the exact use of recently issued 4.45% senior notes has not been officially announced, I would expect some of the proceeds to be used in reducing the total amount outstanding in the year 2021 maturities. If this were to take place, debt maturities would be spread almost perfectly over the course of the next 10 years (the notes that were issued will mature on July 15, 2028).
Source: March Investor Presentation
Core FFO And AFFO Growth When possible, I use adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) as the best way to figure out how quickly a REIT is growing. Part of the reason for using AFFO is that it includes FFO along with any recurring capital expenditures (maintenance expenses typically used to maintain a REITs assets). There are two reasonable assumptions we can make when there is little difference in FFO and AFFO:
The average age of structures are newer or have been recently renovated which means that less capital is needed to maintain the data centers. Management can choose to spend less on maintaining existing structures as a way to temporarily increase cash flow (FFO/AFFO).
Source: April Q1 Report
In order to accurately assess DLR's situation, I have chosen to focus on core FFO and AFFO. The reason for using core FFO is that it excludes one-time and unforeseen expenditures which helps to smooth out some of the drastic FFO movements shown above. Overall, the spread between core FFO and AFFO seem reasonable because of DLR's portfolio that consists of newer data centers (which implies that it doesn't need to invest a significant amount of capital to maintain its data centers at this point in time).
Year-over-year (YoY) growth in Q1-2017/2018 is looking strong when it comes to core FFO and AFFO:
Q1-2018 Core FFO Growth YoY - 7.2% Q1-2018 AFFO Growth YoY - 12.5% Using revised estimates from Q1-2018 earnings, DLR expects to generate core FFO of $6.50-6.60/share. At a current price of $106.82, DLR's price/FFO is approximately 16.1x to 16.4x.
Dividend March saw a 9% increase in the dividend and was the 13th consecutive year of continuous dividend increases. Even more importantly, DLR has seen its adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) payout ratio decreased from 86% in 2014 down to 67% in 2018 (estimate).
Even with this increase in place, DLR's dividend payout is more than safe based on 2018 core FFO outlook of $6.50-6.60 annually. Assuming these figures are accurate, DLR's current quarterly payout of $1.01/share amounts to a new payout ratio of 61-62% payout ratio. If we use AFFO to make the calculation, then we arrive at a current payout ratio closer to 66%.
Preferred Shares For those who are seeking a higher yield and are less focused on capital appreciation will be able to appreciate DLR's preferred shares since ( DLR.PJ ) currently costs $23.62/share, a PAR rate of $25/share, of August 7, 2022.
When shares were first issued, they offered investors a coupon rate of 5.25% but that yield has since been pushed up to 5.56% based on the closing price of $23.62. I believe that DLR.PJ presents the most compelling value of all DLR's preferred shares due to the fact that it has call protection and principal protection that is currently being offered by other preferred shares. Other shares offer a higher coupon rate and current yield, but their current price is well in excess of PAR.
I rate DLR.PJ as a BUY at the current price of $23.62/share and a Strong BUY at anything less than $23.25/share.
Source: Charles Schwab
Conclusion DLR presents investors with the opportunity to generate consistent returns from the tech field while avoiding the complexity of the ever-changing technology field. DLR's management has demonstrated that it is highly capable of balancing growth and dividends which has served investors extremely well over the course of the last 13 years. At this point in time, I only see DLR's business growing as the need for storage and cloud-based solutions become even more necessary for companies of all sizes.
I personally rate DLR a BUY at current prices and a Strong BUY at anything less than $100/share. I believe a fair long-term price for DLR is approximately $120/share or an upside of approximately 12.3% over current prices.
